skill: Applied maths, statistics and scientific practices
expected_level_description: You can: - apply analytical methods including exploratory data analysis and statistical testing to a specific data set, to reach accurate and reliable conclusions - understand and use different performance and accuracy metrics for model validation in data science projects, hypothesis testing and information retrieval - compare selected applied mathematics and statistical methods and identify their differences - access and use the statistical and scientific tools available within the organisation

You can: - identify the appropriate engineering support to design and provide products for the organisation - recognise the processes and tools for cleansing and preparing data, and put reusable processes and checks in place - use different architectures, including cloud and on-premise - use data manipulation and transformation tools
You can: - apply fundamental principles of data ethics and privacy in your work under supervision - share data ethics and privacy risks through appropriate channels

You can: - adopt an inquisitive and curious approach to data - seek out and research new data science techniques to support learning - ask questions to improve your knowledge and learn about data science norms - see possibilities for improvements and innovation

You can: - show an understanding of the organisation and the benefits of data science - collaborate to help identify user needs and develop and deliver data science products - communicate effectively and present analysis and visualisations tailored to your audience

You can: - manage your CPD (continuous professional development) and can link your learning to objectives and organisational goals - confidently talk about the benefits of data science approaches to existing and potential customers - demonstrate a good understanding of key data science techniques, such as machine learning, and you can use them to build data science solutions, including reports, models and dashboards
You can: - write and test scripts and create basic models in one or more languages - collaborate on shared codebases, using a variety of methodologies

You can: - show an awareness of the differences between delivery methods, such as Agile and waterfall, and can propose the most appropriate method to deliver each product - manage your contribution to tasks to fit in with the work of your wider team
You can: - describe the main parts of the health and care system and the services the organisation supports - explain why patient safety and confidentiality matter in your work
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
You can: - work with pseudonymised data and apply disclosure checks before releasing outputs - recognise when linked or detailed data could identify a patient

skill: Safe and fair AI in health care
expected_level_description: You can: - explain how a model can harm patients, for example through bias, drift, or over-reliance on its output - explain why models need validating on the population they will be used with
You can: - explain the difference between a clinical terminology and a classification - recognise common terminologies such as SNOMED CT and ICD
